messages:
sam: Heads-up — noticed a weird UX/telemetry mismatch when a tenant is hitting the v1->v2 fallback. Console preview shows per-route quota delta as 0 but actual runtime is deducting v2 tokens.

julia: Can you paste the request headers and the console screenshot?

sam: Screenshot uploaded in thread (sorry mobile). Header we log client-side: ```Accept-Version: 2```, console shows fallback badge 'v1 compatible' on route, but usage pane shows v2 model in recent traces.

kevin: Hmm. Are we double-mapping quota attribution somewhere? We switched to route-level attribution in the router rewrite last month. If a token goes to fallback variant we should map to the original route's quota bucket, not the variant model's meter.

sam: That's the expectation. But telemetry traces show meter=redwood.v2.tokens for those requests. Example trace id: trace-0a9f.

kevin: Okay can you run this query in prod-telemetry quick: `select meter, count(*) from token_events where trace_id='trace-0a9f'` — curious which tag path is winning.

sam: Ran it, returns `redwood.v2.tokens` and `route=/api/chat/v1/legacy` as tags. So route is correct, meter tag is model variant.

natalie: UX note — console preview currently derives the delta by summing the route's primary meter sample stream and subtracting baseline. If meter tag != route meter we silently show 0 delta because we only query route-meter (fast path). That logic is fragile.

kevin: That explains it. Short-term fix: modify the delta query to join on trace_id and prefer route tag when meters disagree. Longer-term: ensure router emits a canonical quota_key tag that the console always uses.

sam: Agreed. Also worried about billing surface — tenants see 0 delta in preview but get billed for v2 tokens. That's bad.

julia: We should add a console warning if there is any mismatch between 'preview' and 'live' meter samples for the last 24h. Even a subtle orange badge with tooltip: "preview may be stale due to cross-tagging".

natalie: UX applies. But we need an ops signal: alert when >1% of routed requests have meter!=route_meter for a tenant. That would capture regressions.

kevin: Implementation plan: (1) router to emit canonical tag `quota_key=route:<route_id>` on every token event (PR in router-runtime), (2) telemetry pipeline mapping rule to prefer quota_key when present, (3) console delta query to use quota_key join, (4) add mismatch alert + orange toast.

sam: Timeline? This is customer-facing.

kevin: I can open router PR today — low-risk tag add. Telemetry mapping needs one infra release window (ETA 2 days). Console change is small (query switch + badge) — 1 day. Alert rule + playbook — 1/2 day. Total ~3 days if we parallelize.

natalie: I'll draft copy for the toast and tooltip. Suggest messaging: "Preview may not reflect recent automatic fallbacks — investigating. To view live-metered usage, open the raw traces tab."

julia: Also add an immediate mitigator: run a backfill query and show a one-time banner in tenant console: "Preview mismatch detected for last 24h — recalculating. Click to refresh delta." That buys time until the mapping is fixed.

sam: Sounds good. I'll open a customer-facing incident note if billing variance appears while we patch.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by @kevin:router-tagging PR #432 merged to canary — canary rollout started 6/1 15:02 UTC.

kevin: Will monitor canary metrics (meter-tag-discrepancy and token-rate) and post back. If we see unexpected spike in quota attribution, rollback.

natalie: Once router PR is in canary, I can wire the console to prefer `quota_key` if present and surface the badge.

sam: Thank you. Quick follow-up: do we need to notify finance?

julia: FYI finance on-call pinged if projected variance > $500/day. We should estimate impact after backfill before alerting.

kevin: I'll run a 48h backfill for the tenant cohort and post numbers. If >$500/day we loop in finance and CS.

sam: OK — keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
